I think you may need to install `eslint` locally.

@IanVS if ESLint is installed globally, should `--init` check and also install plugins globally and forego `--save-dev`? I can see reasons why it should always install locally, so the current behavior may be intentional. We also might be getting into an issue of transitive plugin dependencies with `eslint-plugin-promise`.

Ergh, sometimes I wish we could disable global installs of eslint altogether, for all the confusion it causes.

I tend to think it would be a bad thing to install plugins globally during `--init`, as even more than ESLint itself they will vary from project to project.  But, I'm not sure the right way to approach this.  Maybe we can try to detect if `--init` was run from a global installation, and if so disable the `Use a popular style guide` option?  Or warn immediately and disable `--init` altogether?  I'm definitely open to ideas and discussion on this one.

> sometimes I wish we could disable global installs of eslint altogether, for all the confusion it causes.

Hear, hear!

> I tend to think it would be a bad thing to install plugins globally during --init, as even more than ESLint itself they will vary from project to project.

I agree. For example, running `eslint --init` in one project could potentially clobber another project's build. Can we encourage local installs and discourage global usage? I don't think we can warn and immediately disable since that would be a breaking change, but perhaps a "proceed at your own risk" warning? Something like

> Using --init from globally-installed ESLint is not recommended and could lead to unexpected behavior with plugins and shareable configs.

Some editor plugins rely on global installation, so we can't really disable it. 

The problem here is that `--init` is installing `standard` locally, which has a peer dependency on ESLint. ESLint isn't installed locally, so npm is warning to install it. I think the only real action needed here is to make `--init` install ESLint locally if it's missing.

Oooo, I like that idea. That will also mitigate the global usage of eslint
as well.

They might not even be aware that it was installed. Although, I guess, since we change plugins to start resolving based on the location of the config file, it will fix immediate issue of not finding plugin.

@ilyavolodin it helps complete the installation without error. It probably makes sense for us to also outputva message letting the user know that we installed ESLint locally for them and suggest that they use that instead of the globally installed version.
I can try to find some time to look at this - interested in learning how `--init` works!

With the changes in my branch, the installation would remain unchanged if ESLint is installed locally, but will look like the following when it isn't: Pre-installation: Post-installation:

Guess the best here to have an `eslint-cli` module as a tiny runner for `eslint` (with pwd changing, etc) and to disable global installation of `eslint`.
